draft.title: Proving triangles congruent
card: Two triangles are congruent if they are exactly the same shape and size. To prove it, you do not measure. You give reasons.
Name each pair of matching sides or angles and give a reason for each, such as 'given', 'common side', 'vertically opposite angles' or 'alternate angles on parallel lines'.

Then state the test. SSS: three pairs of equal sides. SAS: two pairs of equal sides and the equal angle between them. AAS: two pairs of equal angles and a pair of equal sides that are in matching positions. RHS: right angle, hypotenuse and one other pair of equal sides.
Example: in triangles ABC and DEF, AB = DE (given), BC = EF (given) and angle B = angle E (given). The angle lies between the two sides, so the triangles are congruent (SAS).
draft.remember: Give a reason for each matching pair, then name the test that fits them.

a.q: Triangles PQR and XYZ have PQ = XY, QR = YZ and PR = XZ, each given. Which test proves them congruent?
a.why: All three pairs of sides are equal and no angles are used, so the test is SSS. SAS needs an equal angle between two equal sides, and none is given here.
a.clue: Count the pairs of equal sides, and look for any angles.

b.q: In triangles ABC and ADC, AB = AD and BC = DC, each given, and they share side AC. Which test proves they are congruent, with the reason for AC?
opts: SSS, AC is a common side
SAS, AC is a common side
SSS, AC is given as equal
b.why: The triangles have three pairs of equal sides: AB = AD, BC = DC and AC = AC (common side). That is SSS. SAS is tempting, but no angle is known, so it cannot be used.
b.clue: Check whether any angle is known before choosing a test.

b.best: SSS, AC is a common side
